content.comment_body: Hello, I'm working with the [product_no] version of a [product_name]. I want each cursor key to trigger its own timer (for example, if C1 is pressed, timer1 starts; if C2 is pressed simultaneously, timer2 starts). I'm looking for advice on how to allow only one cursor key input and block the rest until the process is complete, or alternatively, how to override ongoing actions if another key is pressed.

Hi [user_name], The [product_no] version of the [product_name] does not support cursor key functionality. Support for cursor keys is available from [product_no] and later versions. Best regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: A user wants to use multiple cursor keys for input, each associated with its own timer. However, the version of [product_name] they're using does not support cursor key inputs. Another participant clarifies that cursor key support is only available in newer hardware versions, highlighting a known constraint.
analysis.user_expectations: User expects to be able to treat each cursor key as a separate input with its own timer and to implement control logic that blocks or overrides other inputs depending on key activity.
